statement: One line holds a non-negative integer n. Print the number formed by reversing its digits. Use the digit loop with an accumulator: start rev at 0, and each pass set rev to rev times 10 plus the last digit of n, then drop that digit from n. Trailing zeros of n vanish naturally - the reverse of 1200 is 21 - because rev is a number and numbers carry no leading zeros. No string conversion is needed, though it is a fine cross-check.
constraints: The reversed value fits comfortably in 64 bits.

example.why: rev grows 3, 32, 321 as the loop pops 3, then 2, then 1 off the right of n.

hint: rev times 10 slides everything collected one place left; the fresh digit fills the gap.
mistake: Padding the reversal with the original's trailing zeros - 0021 is no number; 21 is the answer.
